children: Snap (SNAP) stock rose 2% early Thursday after the company expanded the reach of its Specs augmented-reality glasses through a group of technology and telecom partnerships.

The initiative brings together Nvidia (NVDA), Amazon Web Services (AMZN), Salesforce (CRM), Trifork and Hololight as Snap looks to broaden adoption of its wearable computing platform among business customers.

In the U.S., Snap also said it is working with Verizon (VZ) to provide connectivity plans, financing options and in-store demonstrations. The company said the Specs Connected Case package will be priced at $2,395, while qualified buyers may access installment plans stretching up to 36 months. Monthly wearable data plans start at $10 for Verizon subscribers and $20 for other users.

Separately, Snap introduced Specs Intelligence, an AI-powered service designed for iPhone, Mac and Specs devices. The company said invitation-only early access is now available on Mac, while a preview version can be accessed through the Specs iOS application in the United States.
Snap expects shipments of the glasses to begin later this fall in the U.S., the UK and France. Financial details of the partnerships were not disclosed.

title: Snap Lands Nvidia, Amazon and Salesforce Deals to Supercharge Specs
